title: Latency mosaic: trace hooks, telemetry pipeline, and resilient burn-rate guard
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: We have recurring late-night pages tied to transient tail-latency spikes that the existing burn-rate alarms are either too noisy or too slow to catch. Observability signals are fragmented: traces are sampled inconsistently across services, metric histograms are coarse, and log ingestion drops at peak which blinds SREs during incidents. Goal: implement a cohesive set of tracing hooks, a hardened metrics/log pipeline with graded retention, and a resilient burn-rate guard that reduces pager noise while catching real SLO degradations within the configured burn-rate window. Success metrics: 40% reduction in false-positive P1 pages for request-latency SLOs, median alert time <= configured burn window, and end-to-end trace-to-metric latency <= 12s for critical paths.
comments: 2026-02-20 10:15 - Aisha Patel: Drafted initial spec and impact assessment. Proposed three pillars: (1) trace hook standardization, (2) metrics enrichment pipeline with histogram bucketing, (3) adaptive burn-rate guard that uses trace-derived error attribution.

2026-02-24 14:40 - Architecture review (L. O'Connor, M. Ruiz, S. Chen): Agreed on service-side minimal hook library and centralized enrichment workers. Raised concern about increased cardinality from finer histogram buckets. Action: run cardinality simulation against 7d inertial traffic sample.

2026-02-27 09:03 - Engineering lead (M. Ruiz): Approved phased rollout: instrument core services first (router, inference-gateway, batch-assembler), then infra services. Blocker: need short-term prometheus exporter change (PR #2034) to expose p99/p999 histograms as exemplar metrics.

2026-03-02 16:12 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/2087 - adds trace hook shim + sampling override for SLO probes. QA notes included in PR. Requesting review from observability and runtime teams.

2026-03-05 11:45 - Observability (S. Chen): Completed ingestion pipeline test feeding 1M delta events/hour into staging. Observed 2.2x storage increase with naive histogram expansion. Decided to use dynamic bucketing for top-10 latency paths only.

2026-03-08 07:56 - Canary results: 72h canary on inference-gateway instrumented traffic. Alerts: one true-positive burn-rate triggered (tied to a model swap misconfiguration). False positives: none for the canary slice. Next: expand canary to 20% of production and finalize paging policy wording.

2026-03-12 15:30 - Liam O'Connor: Implemented preliminary burn-rate guard that fuses metric histograms with trace-attributed error tags. Drafted runbook and added grafana dashboard (grafana.redwood.internal/d/latency-mosaic). Planning rollout to production 2026-03-20 if no regressions.

acceptance_criteria: Trace hook library merged and adopted by router + inference-gateway in staging
Metrics pipeline accepts enriched spans and emits p50/p95/p99/p999 histograms with dynamic bucketing for top latency paths
Burn-rate guard triggers alerts with <= 12s end-to-end detection on staged traffic and follows new paging policy templates
Runbook created with triage steps, autorecovery knobs, and rollback instructions
End-to-end tests (synthetic probe) reproduce a gradual SLO burn and demonstrate alert escalation and auto-suppression rules
tasks: Implement enrichment worker that joins traces to metric histograms (ENG-446702-2)
Update Prometheus exporter to support exemplar linking and dynamic histogram bucketing (ENG-446702-3)
Build burn-rate guard service that consumes enriched metrics and applies anomaly filters (ENG-446702-4)
Create Grafana dashboard and alert runbook; link to PagerDuty escalation policy (ENG-446702-5)
Canary rollout: 5% -> 20% -> 100% with blackout windows and storage cost guardrails (ENG-446702-6)
decisions: Use minimal service-side hook (single header + sampling override) rather than heavy SDK to minimize runtime overhead
Adopt dynamic histogram bucketing for only top-10 latency paths to control cardinality and storage
Fuse trace error-attribution with metric burn-rate instead of relying solely on metric thresholding to reduce false positives
Defer full logs-join in the first iteration; surface exemplar trace IDs in metrics for manual correlation
risks: Cardinality blowup if dynamic bucketing misidentifies top latency paths — mitigated by daily re-eval and upper bound caps
Slight CPU overhead on gateway from hook sampling — validated as +1.8% CPU in staging canary, acceptable for P1
Alert regressions due to rollout misconfigurations — mitigated with staged canaries and automatic quiet-hours gating
qa_notes: Run synthetic probe (slo-prober) with injected latency spikes and confirm burn-rate detection within configured window
Verify exemplar links in metrics open the associated trace in trace viewer with <= 2s lookup time
Checkpoint storage increase and validate retention policy enforcement for enriched histograms
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - staging: merge PRs, instrument 3 services, run 72h canary
Phase 1 - small prod canary (5%): monitor false-positive rate and CPU/memory impact for 48h
Phase 2 - expanded canary (20%): enable burn-rate guard alerts for SRE triage only
Phase 3 - full rollout: enable paging per new policy and set auto-suppression thresholds
